title: Cookie, sugar or plain, sugar free

content.title: About
content.content: Sugar‑free cookie is a baked product made from whole‑food ingredients such as whole‑grain flour, nuts, seeds and non‑sugar sweeteners (e.g., stevia or erythritol). It can be sweet or plain but contains no added sugar, making it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar‑free cookies are popular in weight‑loss and low‑glycemic diets.
Non‑sugar sweeteners often have a lower glycemic index than regular sugar.
Traditional sugar‑free recipes used honey, maple syrup or fruit puree, while modern versions rely on artificial sweeteners.
Proper leavening and baking time keep the cookie crisp despite the lack of sugar.
Some sugar‑free cookies are fortified with protein or extra fiber for added nutrition.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Absence of added sugar helps maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and seeds increase dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Nuts and seeds provide mono‑ and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grains and nuts supply B1, B2, B3 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports weight control
items.content: Low sugar combined with protein and fiber promotes satiety.

items.title: Nut and seed allergies
items.content: The cookie may contain nuts, peanuts, sesame or other common allergens.

items.title: Sweetener tolerance
items.content: Some artificial sweeteners (e.g., sorbitol) can cause gas or laxative effects in large amounts.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Even without sugar, cookies can be high in fats and calories, so portion control is important.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: If hydrogenated oils are used, small amounts of trans fats may be present.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sugar‑free cookies are convenient for on‑the‑go snacking, as a mid‑meal bite, or crumbled into yogurt and oatmeal. Pair them with nut butter, cottage cheese, or fruit puree for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat rancidity. Keep moisture out to retain crispness.
